blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Erosion involves both the acquisition and transportation of rock debris by dynamic geomorphic agents.
V-shaped valleys, gorges, and canyons are prominent fluvial erosional landforms formed during the youthful stage of rivers.
Cirques, glacial troughs, hanging valleys, and horns are characteristic features created by glacial erosion.
Karst topography develops predominantly in soluble rocks like limestone and dolomite through continuous solution processes.
Aeolian erosional landforms such as yardangs, zeugens, and mushroom rocks dominate arid and semi-arid landscapes.

blocks.content: Erosion involves the acquisition and transportation of rock debris by geomorphic agents such as running water, wind, glaciers, and waves.

items: Distinguish between Gorges (steep walls, uniform width) and Canyons (stepped slopes, wider at the top than the bottom) for UPSC prelims.
Cirque lakes, also known as Tarns, form when water fills the basin left after glacial ice melts.
Limestone sinkholes, dolines, and blind valleys are frequently asked karst erosional landforms in SSC and State PCS examinations.
